lines.trans: What does that slang word mean now?
Acting cute.
That is what it meant? Read the rest without skipping anything.
You are no longer Cindy, you are Money-dy.
Let's stop here. It is too hard on me.
Hard on you?
Of course it is hard.
And does it not make you feel bad?
Yeah, of course I feel bad.
Then why do you not report them?
We cannot sue over this level. If you look at anti-fan forums, there is far worse stuff.
How do you know that? Are you a member of my anti-fan club?

examples.trans: Did you hear about this acting-cute slang?
I was busy today because of acting-cute slang.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
It really is cute compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is cute and nice.
Did you hear about this pretending?
I was busy today because of pretending.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
I want to filter, skip right now.
How about trying to filter, skip together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.
I want to read right now.
How about trying to read together tomorrow?

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Often used as a command or suggestion to stop.

examples.trans: Please stop now.
Let's stop fighting.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
It really is find it hard, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is find it hard, so and nice.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: commonly paired with 좋다 ('good') or 나쁘다 ('bad')

examples.trans: The weather is clear, so I'm in a good mood.

examples.text: 칭찬을 들으니 기분이 날아갈 것 같아요.
examples.trans: Hearing the compliment makes me feel on cloud nine.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
The weather is bad.
I feel bad.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.
I understand well (of course).
Today is a (of course) busy day.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.
Did you hear about this reporting to police?
I was busy today because of reporting to police.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.
Did you hear about this level, degree?
I was busy today because of level, degree.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
Did you hear about this anti-fan forum?
I was busy today because of anti-fan forum.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun referring to a location.

examples.trans: I have no place to go.
I have no place to go. (2)
I understand well (far, much).
Today is a (far, much) busy day.
The atmosphere today is really worse, more extreme.
That person always looks worse, more extreme.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?
Did you hear about this are you a member??
I was busy today because of are you a member?.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
